description: Details submitted pursuant to reference 25/03492/FUL: tree protection (6), SuDS (7), fire safety (8), refuse and recycling (9), cycle parking  (10), enclosure (11) and external lighting (12) in respect of change of use from bowling club (Class F)  into a cafe (Class E) involving a single storey glazed conservatory
decision_conditions: The information submitted in support of discharging Condition 6 is insufficient and inadequate to demonstrate compliance with the requirements of the condition. The submission fails to provide a comprehensive Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plan that fully address the specified requirements, including details of works within Root Protection Areas, construction methodologies, and protection measures.The submission therefore fails to establish that the development can be undertaken without unacceptable harm to retained trees or the character of the site and is consequently unacceptable, contrary to Policy DM D80 (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

The information submitted in support of discharging Condition 7 is insufficient and inadequate to demonstrate compliance with the requirements of the condition. The submission does not provide a detailed Sustainable Drainage Strategy supported by appropriate technical evidence, including infiltration testing, full design details of sustainable drainage measures, and a management and maintenance plan.The submission therefore fails to demonstrate that surface water will be managed sustainably, that flood risk will be minimised, or that the drainage system will remain functional for the lifetime of the development, and is consequently unacceptable, contrary to Policy CP28 (Managing Flood Risk Through Development) of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policy DMD 61 (Managing Surface Water) of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014), the London Plan (2021), and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The information submitted in support of discharging Condition 8 is insufficient and inadequate to demonstrate compliance with the requirements of the condition. The submission fails to provide a comprehensive Fire Safety Strategy demonstrating how the development will achieve appropriate standards of fire safety, including evacuation arrangements, fire service access, and measures to minimise the risk and spread of fire.The submission therefore fails to ensure that the development would provide an acceptable level of safety for occupants and users and is consequently unacceptable, contrary to Policy D12 (Fire Safety) of the London Plan (2021).

The information submitted in support of discharging Condition 9 is insufficient and inadequate to demonstrate compliance with the requirements of the condition. The submission fails to provide a detailed Waste and Recycling Management Strategy, including sufficient information on storage arrangements, capacity, collection, and measures to mitigate impacts such as litter, odour, and vermin.The submission therefore fails to demonstrate that appropriate waste management arrangements can be achieved without harm to visual amenity, public health, or the character of the area and is consequently unacceptable, contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024) and local plan policies relating to amenity and environmental quality.

The information submitted in support of discharging Condition 10 is insufficient and inadequate to demonstrate compliance with the requirements of the condition. The submission fails to demonstrate that cycle parking provision meets the required number, accessibility, security, and design standards set out in the condition.The submission therefore fails to show that adequate and suitable cycle parking can be provided to support sustainable transport objectives and is consequently unacceptable, contrary to policies within the London Plan (2021) and local plan policies promoting sustainable and active travel.

The information submitted in support of discharging Condition 12 is insufficient and inadequate to demonstrate compliance with the requirements of the condition. The submission is generic in nature and fails to provide sufficient detail in respect of the location, design, luminance levels, and direction of lighting.The submission therefore fails to demonstrate that the proposed lighting would not result in unacceptable impacts on the character of the area, nearby heritage assets, or biodiversity and is consequently unacceptable, contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), policies within the London Plan (2021) relating to design, and local plan policies relating to amenity and environmental protection.
